description: Pooled check over Lessons 6–10 of the Agentic Ai series. Score 80% or higher to unlock the cert prep exam.

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: The biggest agent-ops mistake is picking one 'best' model and pointing everything at it. This lesson builds the three-tier capability model, the three jobs of a router, and the fallback chains that keep agents alive when providers fail.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Designing Tools That Fail Well: Schemas, Error Handling, and Retries”, what is the central focus?

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: A tool is an operational contract, not an API wrapper. This lesson covers the five-part anatomy of a production tool, structured error schemas the model can act on, and retry discipline (backoff with jitter, idempotency keys, and retry budgets), so agents survive failures without corrupting state.

Enterprise agents are connected to production systems, and a vague schema or a blind retry can cause wrong reports, duplicate orders, or operational disruption.

This lesson is about the tools themselves: what separates a demo tool from a production tool is not the happy path; it's how the tool behaves when something goes wrong.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Function-Calling Parity Across OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Gemini, and Local Models”, what is the central focus?

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: Every frontier provider exposes function calling, but none uses the same wire format. This lesson maps the request and response shapes across OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, and Gemini, then shows why local models (llama.cpp) are the parity wildcard and how one internal schema plus thin per-provider adapters keeps an agent portable.

The one idea to take from this lesson: treat your canonical tool schema as the source of truth, and treat each provider's wire format as a dialect your adapter layer translates to and from.
Function-calling parity means understanding those differences well enough to build one internal contract that survives provider swaps.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?

RAG, retrieval-augmented generation, is the single most deployed pattern in enterprise AI, and it is the first one most teams actually ship.
